metadata.name: Zeabur Builder
metadata.description: Builds container images from Git in the cluster, with a Dockerfile or Railpack, and keeps them in zot, an OCI registry installed with it, so builds need no external registry account. Zeabur needs it to deploy services from Git. Optional: without it, services deploy from images only. Nodes pull from zot at the fixed address of the cluster-ip input, and must trust its CA.

inputs.name: cluster-ip
inputs.description: A free address in the cluster's Service CIDR for the registry's Service, such as 10.43.0.50 on k3s and RKE2. Nodes pull through a registry mirror to it. Left out: an address is assigned and only pods reach the registry.

releases.name: tls
releases.manifests:
# Signs the CA below; nothing else uses it.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: zot-selfsigned
  namespace: zot
spec:
  selfSigned: {}
---
# A CA of its own: no public CA signs *.svc names. Nodes and buildkitd
# trust ca.crt from the zot-tls Secret; to use a CA you already
# distribute, point zot-tls at your own issuer instead. Ten years,
# because every node holds a copy and rotating it means redistributing.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: zot-ca
  namespace: zot
spec:
  isCA: true
  commonName: zot-ca
  secretName: zot-ca
  duration: 87600h
  privateKey:
    algorithm: ECDSA
    size: 256
  issuerRef:
    kind: Issuer
    name: zot-selfsigned
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: zot-ca
  namespace: zot
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: zot-ca
---
# The key that signs push tokens. Zeabur Builder reads tls.key and signs
# a short-lived token for each push; zot checks it with tls.crt. Only
# the key matters, so a renewal keeps it (rotationPolicy: Never). zot
# reads tls.crt once at start: to rotate the key, delete the Secret
# zot-token-signer, wait for cert-manager to issue it again, and restart
# zot.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: zot-token-signer
  namespace: zot
spec:
  commonName: zot-token-signer
  secretName: zot-token-signer
  duration: 87600h
  privateKey:
    algorithm: Ed25519
    encoding: PKCS8
    rotationPolicy: Never
  issuerRef:
    kind: Issuer
    name: zot-selfsigned

releases.name: zot
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/project-zot/zot
  tag: v2.1.22@sha256:96cda11459ce6f8c60da3b03f03e9f67fd11b3ae2d82c4c04c92b3c608996080
service:
  # Anyone may pull: never on node ports (the chart's
  # default is NodePort).
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 5000
  # Set by the cluster-ip input; the certificate below names it.
  clusterIP: ""
httpGet:
  # The probes must speak TLS once zot does.
  scheme: HTTPS
# StatefulSet with a volumeClaimTemplate; images survive restarts.
persistence: true
# The restricted Pod Security level. The image has no user of its own,
# so any UID works; fsGroup gives it the volume and the mounted Secrets.
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 65532
  runAsGroup: 65532
  fsGroup: 65532
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault
securityContext:
  # A process gains no privilege that its parent lacks.
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities:
    # zot binds port 5000 and needs no capability.
    drop: [ALL]
extraObjects:
  # The serving certificate; the pod starts once its Secret exists.
  # localhost and 127.0.0.1 let a node pull through a loopback
  # port-forward; the last address is the fixed ClusterIP, or ::1 when
  # there is none. zot reloads the certificate when cert-manager renews
  # it.
  - apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
    kind: Certificate
    metadata:
      name: zot-tls
      namespace: zot
    spec:
      secretName: zot-tls
      dnsNames:
        - zot.zot.svc
        - zot.zot.svc.cluster.local
        - localhost
      ipAddresses:
        - 127.0.0.1
        - '{{ .Values.service.clusterIP | default "::1" }}'
      privateKey:
        algorithm: ECDSA
        size: 256
      issuerRef:
        kind: Issuer
        name: zot-ca
# The chart stores config in a Secret named zot-config and mounts it at
# /etc/zot. configFiles stays empty: the chart refuses both.
configFiles:
  config.json: null
# The chart mounts config from its own Secret; no ConfigMap.
mountConfig: false
# The serving certificate. The pod waits for the Secret.
externalSecrets:
  - secretName: zot-tls
    mountPath: /tls
# Only tls.crt of zot-token-signer, to check tokens: zot never gets
# the key that signs them. The pod waits for the Secret.
extraVolumes:
  - name: token
    secret:
      secretName: zot-token-signer
      items:
        - {key: tls.crt, path: tls.crt}
# bearer.cert reads it from here.
extraVolumeMounts:
  - name: token
    mountPath: /token
    readOnly: true
config:
  # Referrers and artifactType, which source archives use.
  distSpecVersion: 1.1.1
  # No search or UI extensions: they keep an index in memory. No
  # read/write timeouts: the chart's 60s cuts off large layer pushes.
  storage:
    rootDirectory: /var/lib/registry
    dedupe: true
    gc: true
    gcDelay: 2h
    gcInterval: 1h
    # Every untagged manifest goes after the delay; per repository, the
    # 20 most recently pushed tags stay. Builder pushes one tag per
    # commit, so 20 commits remain to roll back to.
    retention:
      delay: 2h
      policies:
        - repositories: ["**"]
          deleteReferrers: true
          deleteUntagged: true
          keepTags:
            - mostRecentlyPushedCount: 20
  http:
    # All interfaces, so the Service reaches the pod.
    address: 0.0.0.0
    # The Service port.
    port: "5000"
    # The certificate and key from the zot-tls Secret.
    tls:
      cert: /tls/tls.crt
      key: /tls/tls.key
    # Pushes, deletes and source reads need a token from Zeabur Builder,
    # signed with the key of zot-token-signer. A token names each
    # repository exactly, such as team-a/api and team-a/api/source, and
    # expires. zot checks such a request against the token alone, not
    # against accessControl. realm is required, but clients send the
    # token without asking it.
    auth:
      bearer:
        realm: https://zot.zot.svc:5000/zot/auth/token
        service: zot
        cert: /token/tls.crt
    # Requests without a token. zot applies the rule with the longest
    # pattern, not the union of matches. Everyone pulls images. Nobody
    # reads source archives (<namespace>/<build>/source).
    accessControl:
      repositories:
        "**":
          anonymousPolicy: [read]
        "**/source":
          policies: []
  # Requests and errors only.
  log:
    level: info

profiles.multi-node:
# Still one replica: filesystem storage has a single writer, and the
# ReadWriteOnce volume binds it to one node anyway.
replicaCount: 1
pvc:
  # More apps building into one registry.
  storage: 50Gi
resources:
  # More concurrent pushes and pulls.
  requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi}
  limits: {memory: 1Gi}
profiles.single-node:
pvc:
  # About 20 builds of a few apps; resize the claim as they grow.
  storage: 20Gi
resources:
  # Idles small without extensions; pushes stream to disk.
  requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 64Mi}
  limits: {memory: 512Mi}

releases.name: builder
releases.values:
registry:
  # zot above: images go to zot.zot.svc:5000/<namespace>/<build>.
  host: zot.zot.svc:5000
  # zot's token signer: each build pushes with a short-lived token for
  # its own repositories only.
  tokenKey:
    namespace: zot
    secret: zot-token-signer
  # buildkitd trusts zot's own CA, copied from the zot-tls Secret at
  # install time.
  caFrom:
    namespace: zot
    secret: zot-tls
  # The egress policy lets buildkitd reach zot's pods on 5000; every
  # other private address stays blocked.
  inCluster:
    namespace: zot
    podLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: zot}
    port: 5000

profiles.single-node:
resources:
  # The controller only; each namespace's buildkitd sizes itself.
  requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 32Mi}
  limits: {memory: 256Mi}
extraArgs:
  # Each namespace's build cache on the node's disk.
  - --buildkitd-cache-size=10Gi

risks.mitigation: Each namespace gets its own buildkitd in a user namespace (Kubernetes 1.33 or later), and its egress policy blocks Pods, Services, nodes and the metadata endpoint. Keep builder-system admin-only, and set runtimeClassName where the cluster has a sandbox such as gVisor or Kata.
risks.risk: buildkitd runs privileged, so a build that escapes its sandbox reaches the node.

risks.mitigation: Keep builder-system admin-only; the controller runs as non-root with no capabilities.
risks.risk: Its token reads and writes every Secret in the cluster.

risks.mitigation: Keep secrets out of images; give them to the workload as Secrets. Pushes, deletes and source reads need a token from Zeabur Builder.
risks.risk: Any pod in the cluster can pull any image anonymously.

risks.mitigation: Keep the zot namespace admin-only. Zeabur Builder reads only this Secret there. If the key leaks, delete the Secret and restart zot once cert-manager has issued a new one.
risks.risk: Whoever reads the Secret zot-token-signer can sign a token for any repository.

risks.mitigation: Zeabur Builder does this on purpose when a Build is deleted. Do not delete every tag of an image by hand unless its sources may go too.
risks.risk: Deleting the last tag of an image repository also removes the repositories below it, such as its source archives in <repository>/source.

risks.mitigation: Set the cluster-ip input, and on every node mirror zot.zot.svc:5000 to https://<cluster-ip>:5000 with ca.crt from the zot-tls Secret as the mirror's CA: k3s or RKE2 registries.yaml (configs.<cluster-ip>:5000.tls.ca_file), or /etc/containerd/certs.d/zot.zot.svc:5000/hosts.toml. zeabur-installer does both. Give buildkitd the same CA; never set insecure_skip_verify.
risks.risk: Nodes refuse to pull until they trust its CA, and a node told to skip verification trusts anything at that address.

security.summary: Zeabur Builder: a ClusterRole that manages Builds, BuildRuns and Jobs in every namespace; reads Pods and Namespaces; reads, creates, updates and deletes Secrets in every namespace (the Git credentials Builds name, and the copies it puts in build namespaces), and reads the zot token signer. Runs one privileged buildkitd per building namespace in its own namespace, with a user namespace and an egress policy. An admission policy limits the Jobs and StatefulSets it can create. zot: no RBAC, a ServiceAccount without roles; serves the OCI registry API over TLS on port 5000 inside the cluster.

releases.name: issuers
releases.manifests:
# Try here first; production rate limits are far lower. Staging
# certificates are not trusted by browsers.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt-staging
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    # No email: ACME accounts need no contact, and Let's Encrypt sends
    # no expiry emails since 2025. Setting spec.acme.email later updates
    # the registered account.
    # Account key, created by cert-manager in its own namespace.
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-staging-account-key
    solvers:
      # HTTP-01 through Traefik's Ingress support; needs no Gateway, and
      # also answers for names served by Gateway listeners. The name
      # must reach port 80 of the cluster from the internet.
      - http01:
          ingress:
            ingressClassName: traefik
---
# Trusted certificates; same settings as staging.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-account-key
    solvers:
      - http01:
          ingress:
            ingressClassName: traefik

metadata.name: Stakater Reloader
metadata.description: Rolls Deployments, StatefulSets and DaemonSets when a ConfigMap or Secret they use changes, whoever changed it. Optional: only workloads that opt in with an annotation restart.

releases.name: reloader
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/stakater/reloader
  tag: v1.4.22@sha256:def2480040adc164b3a57340e77674eadfd88fb7f0593df25e93297f29c7fd7c
reloader:
  # Only workloads annotated reloader.stakater.com/auto or */reload restart.
  autoReloadAll: false
  # Marks the pod template with an annotation instead of adding an
  # environment variable, which the upstream README prefers for Flux and Argo CD.
  reloadStrategy: annotations
  # Leave Jobs alone and never create Jobs from CronJobs; this also drops
  # the chart's batch RBAC rules.
  ignoreJobs: true
  ignoreCronJobs: true
  # Tenants opt in per workload; a namespace list would differ per cluster.
  watchGlobally: true

profiles.multi-node:
reloader:
  # Leader election, so a standby takes over when the leader's node
  # drains. A change made before it holds the Lease (up to 15s) is
  # missed: syncAfterRestart would cover it by rolling every tracked
  # workload on each handoff, so it stays off.
  enableHA: true
  deployment:
    # One leader and one standby.
    replicas: 2
    resources:
      # More ConfigMaps and Secrets to cache.
      requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 128Mi}
      limits: {memory: 512Mi}

risks.mitigation: Set watchGlobally to false and list namespaces: the chart then creates a Role per listed namespace and no ClusterRole. resourceLabelSelector narrows what it caches, not its RBAC.
risks.risk: It reads every Secret in the cluster, so its token exposes all of them.

risks.mitigation: Keep its namespace admin-only; it runs as non-root with the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile.
risks.risk: It can rewrite the pod template of any Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet, including kube-system's.

security.summary: ClusterRole: reads, lists and watches every Secret and ConfigMap; reads, updates and patches Deployments, StatefulSets and DaemonSets; creates Events. Role in its namespace: lists, reads, watches, creates and updates every ConfigMap there, not only its own, and on multi-node the leader-election Lease.

---

metadata: {name: smoke, namespace: catalog-smoke}

  replicas: 1
  args: ["--proactor_threads=1"]
  resources:

    limits: {memory: 512Mi}

    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 999
    runAsGroup: 999
    fsGroup: 999
    seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
  containerSecurityContext:
    allowPrivilegeEscalation: false

metadata.name: External Secrets Operator
metadata.description: Copies values from an external secret store, such as OpenBao, Vault, 1Password or AWS Secrets Manager, into Kubernetes Secrets and keeps them in sync. Optional: it does nothing until you add a SecretStore.

inputs.name: kube-api-cidr
inputs.description: IPv4 CIDR of the Kubernetes API server addresses as the CNI sees them, such as the control-plane node IPs.

releases.name: external-secrets
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; the chart's tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets
  tag: v2.12.0@sha256:7a3c4f7e038fa0f86a3172da19b9388f3f4d846e87e9994ee3474c5b72a9330d
# Off in the chart. Both use the health server on port 8082.
livenessProbe:
  enabled: true
# Ready once the controller has synced its caches.
readinessProbe:
  enabled: true
webhook:
  # The same image as the controller.
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets
    tag: v2.12.0@sha256:7a3c4f7e038fa0f86a3172da19b9388f3f4d846e87e9994ee3474c5b72a9330d
  # Off in the chart. /healthz on port 8081.
  livenessProbe:
    enabled: true
  # cert-manager issues the webhook certificate and injects its CA, so
  # the cert controller and its cluster-wide webhook RBAC are not needed.
  certManager:
    enabled: true
    cert:
      issuerRef:
        group: cert-manager.io
        kind: Issuer
        name: external-secrets-selfsigned
# cert-manager issues the webhook certificate instead.
certController:
  create: false
# Set by the kube-api-cidr input. extraObjects below use it.
kubeApiCidr: ""
extraObjects:
  # Signs the webhook certificate; nothing else uses it.
  - apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
    kind: Issuer
    metadata:
      name: external-secrets-selfsigned
      namespace: external-secrets
    spec:
      selfSigned: {}
  # Deny all traffic in the namespace. The policies below open only the
  # API server and DNS. Add a policy for egress to your secret store.
  - apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: default-deny
      namespace: external-secrets
    spec:
      podSelector: {}
      policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  # Both pods talk to the API server, for watches and leader election.
  - apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: kube-api
      namespace: external-secrets
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchExpressions:
          - key: app.kubernetes.io/name
            operator: In
            values: [external-secrets, external-secrets-webhook]
      policyTypes: [Egress]
      egress:
        - to: [{ipBlock: {cidr: '{{ .Values.kubeApiCidr }}'}}]
          ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 443}, {protocol: TCP, port: 6443}]
  # The controller resolves the secret store host names.
  - apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: dns
      namespace: external-secrets
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: external-secrets}
      policyTypes: [Egress]
      egress:
        - to:
            - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system}}
              podSelector: {matchLabels: {k8s-app: kube-dns}}
          ports: [{protocol: UDP, port: 53}, {protocol: TCP, port: 53}]
  # The API server calls the validating webhook.
  - apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: webhook
      namespace: external-secrets
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: external-secrets-webhook}
      policyTypes: [Ingress]
      ingress:
        - from: [{ipBlock: {cidr: '{{ .Values.kubeApiCidr }}'}}]
          ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 10250}]

profiles.multi-node:
# One leader and one standby, so a node drain does not stop syncs.
replicaCount: 2
# Only the leader reconciles.
leaderElect: true
# More namespaces and Secrets to cache.
resources:
  requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 128Mi}
  limits: {cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi}
webhook:
  # Two replicas: with failurePolicy Fail, no webhook means no writes
  # to its CRDs.
  replicaCount: 2
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 32Mi}
    limits: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}

security.credentialsNote: Each SecretStore names a Secret, or a ServiceAccount, that holds its credentials for the external store. None is created by default.

risks.mitigation: Keep its namespace admin-only. Both pods run as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, no capabilities and the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile. The namespace denies all traffic except to the API server and DNS.
risks.risk: Its token can read and write every Secret in the cluster.

risks.mitigation: Prefer a SecretStore per namespace with credentials scoped to that tenant. On a ClusterSecretStore, set spec.conditions to the namespaces that may use it.
risks.risk: A ClusterSecretStore without conditions serves every namespace: any user who can create an ExternalSecret can read every key the store's credentials reach.

risks.mitigation: Give the store credentials read-only access unless you use PushSecret.
risks.risk: A PushSecret writes a Secret of its namespace into the external store, overwriting what is there.

risks.mitigation: Set rbac.serviceAccountTokenCreate to false and add a Role with resourceNames per ServiceAccount that a SecretStore uses.
risks.risk: It creates a token for any ServiceAccount a SecretStore names, in that SecretStore's namespace.

risks.mitigation: Add a NetworkPolicy in the external-secrets namespace with egress to the store's address and port only, for pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/name=external-secrets.
risks.risk: The controller cannot reach your secret store until you allow it.

The webhook has no RBAC. The chart aggregates read access to its CRDs into view, and write access into edit and admin.

metadata.name: Keel
metadata.description: Rolls workloads annotated keel.sh/policy to a new image tag when Zeabur Builder calls its webhook after a push, or when polling finds one. Optional: only annotated workloads change.

image:

  repository: ghcr.io/keel-hq/keel

  runAsNonRoot: true
  seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
containerSecurityContext:

spec:

    matchLabels: {app: keel}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]

risks.mitigation: Keep its namespace admin-only; it runs as non-root with the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile and no capabilities.
risks.risk: It reads every Secret in the cluster, so its token exposes all of them.

risks.mitigation: The NetworkPolicy keel-webhook lets only pods in builder-system and keel reach 9300; the cluster's CNI must enforce NetworkPolicy. If Zeabur Builder runs in another namespace, change the policy. basicauth with AUTHENTICATED_WEBHOOKS=true (extraEnv) makes every webhook but /v1/webhooks/registry require it; basicauth also enables the admin UI, which otherwise does not exist.
risks.risk: Port 9300 takes webhooks without credentials: whoever can call it rolls any annotated workload, in any namespace, to any tag of that workload's repository.

security.summary: ClusterRole: reads, lists and watches every Secret (registry credentials of tracked workloads), Namespace and Node; reads, updates and deletes Pods, ReplicaSets, ReplicationControllers, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs and CronJobs in every namespace.

smoke.name: rolls-on-native-webhook
smoke.manifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: smoke
  namespace: catalog-smoke
  annotations: {keel.sh/policy: force}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: smoke}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: smoke}}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: pause
          image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9
---
# Retries until Keel has seen the Deployment; a repeated event is a no-op.
# In Keel's namespace: the NetworkPolicy refuses catalog-smoke.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: webhook, namespace: keel}
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: curl
          image: curlimages/curl:8.23.0
          command: [sh, -c]
          args:
            - for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -sSf -d '{"name":"registry.k8s.io/pause","tag":"3.10"}' http://keel.keel.svc:9300/v1/webhooks/native; sleep 10; done

metadata.name: Traefik Proxy
metadata.description: Serves Gateway API and Ingress, and hosts the CrowdSec bouncer. Ingress NGINX was retired in March 2026.

alternatives.envoy-gateway: Serves Gateway API on Envoy; an existing installation is reused.

releases.name: traefik
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: traefik
  tag: v3.7.16@sha256:c8a121e4bb1347e8fd52657fab12f2cb70b68f8a018895e2068f92c9e519b9c2
providers:
  kubernetesGateway:
    # Route web services with HTTPRoute.
    enabled: true
  kubernetesIngress:
    # Many charts still ship Ingress objects.
    enabled: true
  kubernetesCRD:
    # Middleware objects, such as the CrowdSec bouncer.
    enabled: true
    # No references to other namespaces.
    allowCrossNamespace: false
    # Only the traefik namespace can set the default TLS store.
    defaultTLSResourcesNamespace: traefik
gatewayClass:
  # Gateways reference GatewayClass "traefik".
  enabled: true
  name: traefik
gateway:
  # Gateways and listeners are created per domain, not by the chart.
  enabled: false
api:
  # Unauthenticated surface; not needed.
  dashboard: false
service:
  spec:
    # Skip source NAT so Traefik sees client addresses (CrowdSec, rate
    # limits, logs); only nodes running Traefik serve traffic.
    externalTrafficPolicy: Local
accessLog:
  # JSON access logs for metrics, log search and CrowdSec.
  enabled: true
  format: json
  fields:
    # Keep only the fields below; secrets live in headers and queries.
    defaultMode: drop
    names:
      ClientHost: keep
      RequestHost: keep
      RequestMethod: keep
      RequestPath: keep
      RequestProtocol: keep
      DownstreamStatus: keep
      DownstreamContentSize: keep
      RequestContentSize: keep
      Duration: keep
      RouterName: keep
      StartUTC: keep
    headers:
      # Headers carry cookies and bearer tokens.
      defaultMode: drop
    queryParameters:
      # Query strings carry OAuth codes and signed-URL secrets.
      defaultMode: drop

profiles.multi-node:
deployment:
  # One pod per node, so every node keeps client addresses under the
  # Local traffic policy; k3s ServiceLB source-NATs on nodes without one.
  # From a Deployment, annotate it helm.sh/resource-policy=keep before the
  # upgrade and delete it after, or ingress drops for a few seconds.
  kind: DaemonSet
tolerations:
  # The taints k3s ServiceLB tolerates, so Traefik runs wherever it listens.
  - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
    operator: Exists
    effect: NoSchedule
  - key: CriticalAddonsOnly
    operator: Exists
metrics:
  prometheus:
    # Request rate and latency metrics.
    service:
      enabled: true
resources:
  # Headroom for higher request rates.
  requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
  limits: {memory: 512Mi}
profiles.single-node:
deployment:
  # A second copy gains nothing on one node.
  replicas: 1
resources:
  # Idles near 40Mi; the limit contains leaks.
  requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
  limits: {memory: 256Mi}

metadata.name: CrowdSec
metadata.description: Blocks brute-force attempts and scanners that show up in Traefik's access logs, for every app behind the ingress. It fails open, and the online API is off by default.

inputs.name: bouncer-key
inputs.description: The Traefik bouncer uses this key to call the CrowdSec local API.

inputs.name: lapi-secret
inputs.description: The local API (LAPI) signs agent sessions with this shared secret.

inputs.name: registration-token
inputs.description: Agents register with the local API using this token.

releases.name: crowdsec
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: crowdsecurity/crowdsec
  tag: v1.8.1@sha256:0f2523fa61ef507f15d953045cface490cc880670c62f2755ced17524107f71a
# The runtime on k3s and mainstream distributions.
container_runtime: containerd
secrets:
  externalSecret:
    # Inputs, not chart-generated, so every render is identical.
    name: crowdsec-lapi
agent:
  acquisition:
    # Traefik's JSON access log.
    - namespace: traefik
      podName: traefik-*
      program: traefik
  env:
    # Parsers and scenarios for Traefik plus generic HTTP attacks.
    - name: COLLECTIONS
      value: crowdsecurity/traefik
lapi:
  env:
    # No data leaves the cluster unless the user opts in.
    - name: DISABLE_ONLINE_API
      value: "true"
    # Registers the Traefik bouncer (input bouncer-key).
    - name: BOUNCER_KEY_traefik
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef: {name: crowdsec-bouncer-key, key: key}
  persistentVolume:
    data:
      # SQLite decisions and bouncer registrations.
      enabled: true
    config:
      # Keeps machine credentials stable across restarts.
      enabled: true

releases.name: bouncer-middleware
releases.manifests:
# Referenced from Traefik's entrypoints as crowdsec-bouncer@kubernetescrd.
apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
kind: Middleware
metadata:
  name: bouncer
  namespace: crowdsec
spec:
  plugin:
    crowdsec-bouncer:
      enabled: true
      # Local copy of decisions; requests never wait on LAPI.
      crowdsecMode: stream
      crowdsecLapiScheme: http
      crowdsecLapiHost: crowdsec-service.crowdsec.svc.cluster.local:8080
      # Read from the Secret in the Middleware's namespace.
      crowdsecLapiKey: urn:k8s:secret:crowdsec-bouncer-key:key
      # Fail open: if LAPI is unreachable, keep serving traffic.
      updateMaxFailure: -1

contributes.values:
experimental:
  plugins:
    # Downloaded from plugins.traefik.io at start.
    crowdsec-bouncer:
      moduleName: github.com/maxlerebourg/crowdsec-bouncer-traefik-plugin
      version: v1.8.1
ports:
  web:
    http:
      # Every request passes the bouncer; no app opts in.
      middlewares: [crowdsec-bouncer@kubernetescrd]
  websecure:
    http:
      # Same as web.
      middlewares: [crowdsec-bouncer@kubernetescrd]
accessLog:
  fields:
    names:
      # CrowdSec's scenarios key on the client address.
      ClientHost: keep
    headers:
      names:
        # Bot scenarios match on the user agent.
        User-Agent: keep

risks.mitigation: Only administrators manage decisions. Configure trusted proxies before running CrowdSec behind a CDN.
risks.risk: A ban on a shared IP (NAT, CDN) blocks it for every tenant.

metadata.name: VictoriaLogs
metadata.description: Keeps and searches log history with low memory and disk use. It is Apache-2.0, unlike Loki, and runs on the VictoriaMetrics operator.

alternatives.loki: Licensed AGPL-3.0; an existing installation is reused.

releases.name: logs
releases.manifests:
# The log store.
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1
kind: VLSingle
metadata:
  name: victoria-logs
  namespace: observability
spec:
  # Two weeks, or less when the volume reaches 8GiB of its 10Gi.
  retentionPeriod: 14d
  retentionMaxDiskSpaceUsageBytes: 8GiB
  storage:
    resources:
      requests: {storage: 10Gi}
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
    limits: {memory: 1Gi}
---
# One collector per node, reading container logs.
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1
kind: VLAgent
metadata:
  name: collector
  namespace: observability
spec:
  k8sCollector:
    enabled: true
    # Namespace, pod and container suffice; labels add cardinality.
    includePodLabels: false
  remoteWrite:
    - url: http://vlsingle-victoria-logs.observability.svc:9428/internal/insert
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 32Mi}
    limits: {memory: 256Mi}
---
# Only the collector, the metrics stack's vmagent (the operator's scrape of
# /metrics) and Zeabur Proxy in the zeabur namespace reach the log store.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: victoria-logs
  namespace: observability
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vlsingle, app.kubernetes.io/instance: victoria-logs}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - ports: [{port: 9428, protocol: TCP}]
      from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vlagent, app.kubernetes.io/instance: collector}
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmagent}
        # Both selectors: anyone can label a pod in their own namespace.
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: zeabur}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: zeabur-proxy}

risks.mitigation: A NetworkPolicy lets only the collector, vmagent and Zeabur Proxy reach it; tenants query through Zeabur Proxy, which filters by namespace.
risks.risk: The log store holds every tenant's logs in one place.

risks.mitigation: VictoriaLogs drops a line whose stream fields repeat, so it never lands under another namespace; re-run Zeabur Proxy's canary test on upgrades.
risks.risk: The collector adds a pod's JSON log fields to the line, so a pod can print kubernetes.pod_namespace to pose as another namespace.

security.summary: The collector reads pod metadata and node log files.

              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              backup: [metadata, name]
            metrics:

                    path: [status, conditions]
                    labelsFromPath:
                      type: [type]
                      reason: [reason]

          - groupVersionKind: {group: velero.io, version: v1, kind: Backup}

releases.name: notifications
releases.manifests:
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1beta1
kind: VMRule
metadata:
  name: zeabur-notifications
  namespace: observability
spec:
  groups:
    - name: zeabur-project
      interval: 30s
      rules:
        - alert: ZeaburBuildFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, build, buildrun, reason) (
              zeabur_builder_buildrun_completion_time{phase="Failed"}
            ) > time() - 900
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: build-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Build {{ $labels.build }} failed ({{ $labels.reason }})."
            description: "BuildRun {{ $labels.buildrun }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed with reason {{ $labels.reason }}."
        - alert: ZeaburBuildSucceeded
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, build, buildrun) (
              zeabur_builder_buildrun_completion_time{phase="Succeeded"}
            ) > time() - 900
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: build-succeeded, zeabur_kind: event, severity: info}
          annotations:
            summary: "Build {{ $labels.build }} succeeded."
            description: "BuildRun {{ $labels.buildrun }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} succeeded."
        # The Deployment controller gives up on a rollout after
        # progressDeadlineSeconds (600 by default).
        - alert: ZeaburDeployFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, deployment) (
              kube_deployment_status_condition{condition="Progressing", status="false"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: deploy-failed, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Deployment of {{ $labels.deployment }} failed."
            description: "The rollout of {{ $labels.deployment }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} passed its progress deadline."
        # A rollout makes a new ReplicaSet. It succeeded when the
        # Deployment then runs only up-to-date, available replicas. A
        # rollback to an earlier ReplicaSet does not count.
        - alert: ZeaburDeploySucceeded
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, deployment) (
              label_replace(
                (time() - kube_replicaset_created < 1800)
                * on (namespace, replicaset) group_left (owner_name)
                kube_replicaset_owner{owner_kind="Deployment"},
                "deployment", "$1", "owner_name", "(.+)"
              )
            )
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_observed_generation == kube_deployment_metadata_generation)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_updated == kube_deployment_spec_replicas)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available == kube_deployment_spec_replicas)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas == kube_deployment_spec_replicas)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_spec_replicas > 0)
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: deploy-succeeded, zeabur_kind: event, severity: info}
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.deployment }} is deployed."
            description: "All replicas of {{ $labels.deployment }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} run the new version."
        - alert: ZeaburCrashLooping
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, pod, container) (
              kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason="CrashLoopBackOff"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 5m
          labels: {zeabur_event: crash-loop, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.pod }} keeps crashing."
            description: "Container {{ $labels.container }} of {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has been in CrashLoopBackOff for 5 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburOutOfMemory
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, pod, container) (
              kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace, pod, container) (
              max by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[10m])) > 0
            )
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: out-of-memory, zeabur_kind: event, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.pod }} ran out of memory."
            description: "Container {{ $labels.container }} of {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} used its memory limit and restarted."
        # Without the phase in the grouping, a move from one unhealthy
        # phase to another does not restart the 15 minutes.
        - alert: ZeaburPostgresUnhealthy
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster) (
              zeabur_cnpg_cluster_phase{phase!="Cluster in healthy state"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 15m
          labels: {zeabur_event: database-unhealthy, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "PostgreSQL {{ $labels.cluster }} is not healthy."
            description: "PostgreSQL cluster {{ $labels.cluster }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has not been healthy for 15 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburMongoDBUnhealthy
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster) (zeabur_psmdb_state{state="error"}) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: database-unhealthy, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "MongoDB {{ $labels.cluster }} is in error."
            description: "MongoDB cluster {{ $labels.cluster }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has been in error for 10 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburPostgresBackupFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster, backup) (
              zeabur_cnpg_backup_created{phase=~"failed|walArchivingFailing"}
            ) > time() - 21600
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} of PostgreSQL {{ $labels.cluster }} failed."
            description: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
        - alert: ZeaburMongoDBBackupFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster, backup) (
              zeabur_psmdb_backup_created{state=~"error|rejected"}
            ) > time() - 21600
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} of MongoDB {{ $labels.cluster }} failed."
            description: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
        - alert: ZeaburVolumeBackupFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, backup) (
              zeabur_k8up_backup_condition_time{type="Completed", reason="Failed"}
            ) > time() - 21600
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Volume backup {{ $labels.backup }} failed."
            description: "K8up backup {{ $labels.backup }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
        # Volumes on local-path report no usage; this covers the others.
        - alert: ZeaburVolumeAlmostFull
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (
              kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes
            ) < 0.1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: volume-almost-full, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} is almost full."
            description: "Less than 10% of volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} is free."
        # cert-manager renews 30 days before expiry, so 14 days left
        # means renewal keeps failing.
        - alert: ZeaburCertificateExpiring
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, certificate) (zeabur_certmanager_certificate_not_after) - time() < 14 * 86400
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: certificate, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} expires soon."
            description: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} expires in less than 14 days and was not renewed."
        - alert: ZeaburCertificateNotReady
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, certificate) (zeabur_certmanager_certificate_condition{type="Ready"}) == 0
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 1h
          labels: {zeabur_event: certificate, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} is not ready."
            description: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has not been issued for an hour."
        # Zeabur creates a short-lived Job with this label to test a
        # channel. The namespace comes from the Job, so a person can
        # only test the channels of a namespace where they create Jobs.
        - alert: ZeaburNotificationTest
          expr: |
            label_replace(
              max by (namespace, label_zeabur_com_notification_test) (
                kube_job_labels{label_zeabur_com_notification_test!=""}
              ),
              "zeabur_channel", "$1", "label_zeabur_com_notification_test", "(.+)"
            )
          labels: {zeabur_event: test, zeabur_kind: event, severity: info}
          annotations:
            summary: "Test notification from Zeabur."
            description: "This channel receives notifications from {{ $labels.namespace }}."
    - name: zeabur-cluster
      interval: 30s
      # The cluster's channels are in observability.
      labels: {namespace: observability}
      rules:
        - alert: ZeaburNodeNotReady
          expr: |
            max by (node) (kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="true"}) == 0
          for: 5m
          labels: {zeabur_event: node-not-ready, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Node {{ $labels.node }} is not ready."
            description: "Node {{ $labels.node }} has not been ready for 5 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburNodeDiskAlmostFull
          expr: |
            max by (instance, mountpoint) (
              node_filesystem_avail_bytes{fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs"}
            ) < 0.1
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: volume-almost-full, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Disk {{ $labels.mountpoint }} on {{ $labels.instance }} is almost full."
            description: "Less than 10% of {{ $labels.mountpoint }} on {{ $labels.instance }} is free."
        - alert: ZeaburSystemCrashLooping
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, pod, container) (
                kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason="CrashLoopBackOff"}
              ) == 1
              unless on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""},
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          for: 5m
          labels: {zeabur_event: crash-loop, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "System pod {{ $labels.pod }} keeps crashing."
            description: "Container {{ $labels.container }} of {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.object_namespace }} has been in CrashLoopBackOff for 5 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburSystemVolumeAlmostFull
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (
                kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes
              ) < 0.1
              unless on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""},
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: volume-almost-full, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} is almost full."
            description: "Less than 10% of volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} in {{ $labels.object_namespace }} is free."
        - alert: ZeaburSystemCertificateExpiring
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, certificate) (zeabur_certmanager_certificate_not_after) - time() < 14 * 86400
              unless on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""},
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          labels: {zeabur_event: certificate, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} expires soon."
            description: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} in {{ $labels.object_namespace }} expires in less than 14 days and was not renewed."
        - alert: ZeaburClusterBackupFailed
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, backup) (
                zeabur_velero_backup_created{phase=~"Failed|PartiallyFailed|FailedValidation"}
              ) > time() - 21600,
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Cluster backup {{ $labels.backup }} failed."
            description: "Velero backup {{ $labels.backup }} did not complete."
---
# Only the alert senders and the scraper reach Alertmanager. Without
# this, any pod could post alerts with another project's namespace, or
# silence them. kubectl port-forward does not pass through
# NetworkPolicies, so it still works.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: vmalertmanager-senders-only
  namespace: observability
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmalertmanager}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmalert}
      ports:
        - {port: 9093, protocol: TCP}
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: falco}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: falcosidekick}
      ports:
        - {port: 9093, protocol: TCP}
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmagent}
      ports:
        - {port: 9093, protocol: TCP}
        - {port: 8435, protocol: TCP}
    # Replicas gossip silences and notification state.
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmalertmanager}
      ports:
        - {port: 9094, protocol: TCP}
        - {port: 9094, protocol: UDP}

falcosidekick:
  config:
    alertmanager:
      # Falco alerts go to the cluster's channels only: they carry
      # command lines from every namespace.
      hostport: http://vmalertmanager-vm-victoria-metrics-k8s-stack.observability.svc:9093
      # The chart's default is the v1 API, which Alertmanager 0.27 removed.

      # Notices are frequent and rarely need action.

      # A Falco alert has no end. It ends 10 minutes after the last one.

metadata.name: Tailscale Kubernetes operator
metadata.description: Puts a Service or Ingress on the tailnet with no port open to the internet. An Ingress gets a MagicDNS name with a Let's Encrypt certificate, so a host without a domain still serves trusted HTTPS; a Service is proxied as it is, without TLS. Optional: it needs a Tailscale account, and an Ingress needs HTTPS and MagicDNS enabled on the tailnet.

inputs.name: oauth-client-id

inputs.name: oauth-client-secret
inputs.description: The operator authenticates with this OAuth client secret.

  clientSecret: ""

  image:

    repository: tailscale/k8s-operator
    tag: v1.104.2@sha256:9cddfcbe75a7eab2b46d610966d519a28699a5e38235a2cb3aec960487c4aa48

risks.risk: Anyone who can create a Service or Ingress in any namespace can put it on the tailnet (annotation tailscale.com/expose, loadBalancerClass tailscale, or IngressClass tailscale), or reach a tailnet device through an egress Service (annotation tailscale.com/tailnet-fqdn).

risks.mitigation: A DNSConfig and a CoreDNS stub domain for ts.net resolve names that have an egress proxy; an Ingress needs the experimental annotation tailscale.com/experimental-forward-cluster-traffic-via-ingress, which makes its proxy privileged. Calling the in-cluster Service avoids both.

metadata.name: Longhorn
metadata.description: Block storage replicated across nodes: a volume survives losing its node, follows its pod to another node, and can be expanded in place. Recommended on multi-node, where it becomes the default storage class. Optional on single-node, where a replica has nowhere else to go; it still gives expandable volumes and snapshots there.

alternatives.local-path: What the cluster has without it. Faster, but a volume stays on the node that created it. Still the better class for databases that replicate themselves (CloudNativePG, MongoDB): a second layer of copies costs write latency and disk for nothing.

releases.name: longhorn
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  longhorn:
    manager:
      repository: longhornio/longhorn-manager
      tag: v1.13.0@sha256:7372f3c59239e9a67c0017b3af32fabdf08c4dcc0631140161da9a47e3b142f0
    shareManager:
      repository: longhornio/longhorn-share-manager
      tag: v1.13.0@sha256:53950f78b7af38b8a943c298cd3020622191a4661a13036f69d83c154cc8690d
    ui:
      repository: longhornio/longhorn-ui
      tag: v1.13.0@sha256:f22fb0254ae50195c1635ce428dfae26375956b3d7bd39640fae8fe33a236023
persistence:
  # One copy per node, up to three: losing a node leaves two while the
  # third rebuilds. Two nodes give two copies; with one down, volumes
  # run on a single copy until it is back.
  defaultClassReplicaCount: 3
  # Volumes outlive their claims only when a person asks for it, as with local-path.
  reclaimPolicy: Delete
defaultSettings:
  # With fewer nodes than replicas, volumes still attach (degraded) and gain
  # their missing replicas as nodes join, so a class asking for 3 gives
  # min(3, nodes) copies.
  allowVolumeCreationWithDegradedAvailability: true
  # Spread existing replicas onto nodes that join later.
  replicaAutoBalance: best-effort
  # No calls to Longhorn's upgrade server; versions change with the catalog.
  upgradeChecker: false
  allowCollectingLonghornUsageMetrics: false
  # After a Longhorn upgrade, move attached volumes to the new engine one
  # node at a time; otherwise they stay on the old one until done by hand.
  concurrentAutomaticEngineUpgradePerNodeLimit: 1
longhornUI:
  # No login: it acts as Longhorn's admin. ClusterIP only (the chart's
  # default, no Ingress); reach it with kubectl port-forward.
  replicas: 1
longhornManager:
  resources:
    # The chart sets none. No limit: killing the manager stalls attach
    # and detach on its node.
    requests: {cpu: 25m, memory: 128Mi}

profiles.multi-node:
persistence:
  # New volumes without a class survive losing a node. local-path stays
  # available for databases that replicate themselves.
  defaultClass: true
defaultSettings:
  # A pod on a dead node otherwise holds its volume until someone
  # force-deletes it; this lets it start elsewhere.
  nodeDownPodDeletionPolicy: delete-both-statefulset-and-deployment-pod
profiles.single-node:
persistence:
  # local-path stays the default: on one node it is faster, and
  # Longhorn is for volumes that need to grow.
  defaultClass: false
  # One node: a second replica would sit on the same disk.
  defaultClassReplicaCount: 1
csi:
  # One node: the chart's three replicas of each sidecar gain nothing.
  attacherReplicaCount: 1
  provisionerReplicaCount: 1
  resizerReplicaCount: 1
  snapshotterReplicaCount: 1
longhornGlobalManager:
  # One node: the chart's three warm standbys gain nothing.
  replicas: 1

metadata.name: Velero
metadata.description: Backs up the whole cluster to S3 for disaster recovery. It can touch any namespace, so it is for administrators only.

alternatives.k8up: Backs up each namespace on its own, so tenants can use it.

inputs.name: bucket
inputs.description: Velero stores backups in this S3 bucket.

inputs.name: s3-url
inputs.description: Velero connects to this S3 endpoint URL; any S3-compatible service works.

inputs.name: credentials
inputs.description: Velero reads the bucket's credentials from this AWS-style credentials file.

inputs.name: repository-password
inputs.description: Kopia encrypts file-system backups with this password. Without the Secret, Velero uses its built-in password, which is public.

inputs.name: backup-key
inputs.description: The S3 server encrypts every backup object, Secrets included, with this SSE-C key. The AWS plugin needs exactly 32 bytes.

inputs.name: file-backup
inputs.description: Off by default. Set true to install the node agent on every node, so Velero can copy volume files with Kopia. The agent runs as root, mounts host paths, holds Velero's cluster-admin token, and needs the velero namespace to allow the privileged Pod Security level. Each Backup and Schedule must then set defaultVolumesToFsBackup to true. Zeabur's schedule does. While the input is false, such a backup fails partly.

releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.

  tag: v1.18.2@sha256:37396519f399536e5f01427d723565ae69294ec3fb5625cf1c87c09eaa9de16b
initContainers:

      - mountPath: /target
        name: plugins
credentials:
  # Secret comes from the credentials input, not the chart.
  useSecret: true
  existingSecret: velero-credentials
configuration:
  backupStorageLocation:
    # One S3 location; bucket and URL are inputs.
    - name: default
      provider: aws
      default: true
      config:
        region: us-east-1
        s3ForcePathStyle: "true"
        # Velero writes Secrets into the backup as they are. The
        # store encrypts them with the backup-key input (SSE-C).
        customerKeyEncryptionSecret: velero-backup-key/key
  # Kopia file-system backups work on any storage class, local-path included.
  uploaderType: kopia
  # No node agent by default, so no volume copy. Backups opt in with file-backup.
  defaultVolumesToFsBackup: false
# CSI snapshots need per-driver setup; use file-system backups instead.
snapshotsEnabled: false

security.credentialsNote: Needs static S3 credentials. All backups share one Kopia password and one SSE-C key, both in Secrets in the velero namespace.

risks.mitigation: Never grant Velero CRDs to tenants.
risks.risk: Backups and Restores can include any namespace, including other tenants' Secrets.

risks.mitigation: Take one backup by hand after install, then download backups/<name>/velero-backup.json without the key: the store must refuse it. SeaweedFS supports SSE-C.
risks.risk: SSE-C sends the key with each request, so the S3 server sees the backup before it encrypts it. A store without SSE-C refuses the uploads, or ignores the key and keeps the backups in clear text.

risks.mitigation: Keep a copy of both Secrets outside the cluster. Before a restore into a new cluster, create them first.
risks.risk: Without the velero-repo-credentials and velero-backup-key Secrets, nobody can read the backups. Both are also inside the backups that they encrypt.

security.summary: Bound to cluster-admin; reads and restores every object. By default no Pod is privileged and the velero namespace needs only the baseline Pod Security level. With the file-backup input, a root node agent on every node holds the same token, mounts host paths and needs the privileged level.

upgradeNotes.note: Upgrade the AWS plugin together with Velero.

If Velero ran before velero-repo-credentials existed, Velero made it with its public default password, and Kopia keeps the password of a repository. Point the location at a new prefix to start encrypted repositories. Backups made before SSE-C stay unencrypted.

metadata.name: Browserless
metadata.description: Authenticated headless Chromium service for trusted automation clients, with restricted container isolation. Browserless is SSPL-1.0 (https://github.com/browserless/browserless/blob/main/LICENSE), which is not OSI-approved; closed-source commercial sites, apps or CI may need a commercial license.

inputs.name: token
inputs.description: Generated Browserless bearer/query token. Retrieve from browserless-secrets/token through authorized Kubernetes access; never put the value in a URL logged by a proxy.

security.summary: Browserless runs as a restricted non-root container with a read-only filesystem. Its API needs a token, and the pod has no Kubernetes service-account token. Outbound traffic is not limited. Do not share one instance between tenants you do not trust.

zh-CN.summary: Browserless 以受限的非 root 身份运行，文件系统只读。API 需要 token 才能调用，Pod 也没有 Kubernetes 服务账号 token。对外连接没有限制。不要让互不信任的租户共用同一个实例。

zh-TW.summary: Browserless 以受限的非 root 身分執行，檔案系統唯讀。API 需要 token 才能呼叫，Pod 也沒有 Kubernetes 服務帳號 token。對外連線沒有限制。不要讓彼此不信任的租戶共用同一個實例。

risks.risk: The browser starts with --no-sandbox, because upstream launches Chromium that way. If a website exploits the browser, the attacker can take over the container, read its Browserless token and see what other browser sessions show.
risks.mitigation: Let only trusted clients call the API. Keep the image patched. For sensitive browsing, run this service in its own tenant namespace on dedicated nodes. Keep the restricted admission policy, and do not grant SYS_ADMIN or host access. Do not share one instance between tenants you do not trust.

zh-CN.risk: 浏览器启动时带有 --no-sandbox，因为上游就是这样启动 Chromium。如果有网站攻破浏览器，攻击者就能控制容器，拿到 Browserless token，也能看到其他浏览器会话的内容。
zh-CN.mitigation: 只让可信的客户端调用 API。镜像要持续更新。处理敏感内容时，请把这个服务放在自己的租户命名空间，并使用专用节点。保留受限的准入策略，不要授予 SYS_ADMIN 或主机访问权限。不要让互不信任的租户共用同一个实例。

zh-TW.risk: 瀏覽器啟動時帶有 --no-sandbox，因為上游就是這樣啟動 Chromium。如果有網站攻破瀏覽器，攻擊者就能控制容器，拿到 Browserless token，也能看到其他瀏覽器工作階段的內容。
zh-TW.mitigation: 只讓信任的用戶端呼叫 API。映像檔要持續更新。處理敏感內容時，請把這個服務放在自己的租戶命名空間，並使用專用節點。保留受限的准入政策，不要給 SYS_ADMIN 或主機存取權。不要讓彼此不信任的租戶共用同一個實例。

risks.risk: Anyone who can use the browser API can make the server open internal addresses (SSRF). Browserless can block private networks by itself, but that is off by default.
risks.mitigation: The file protocol, GET-style browser calls and CORS are disabled. The template does not limit outbound traffic, so the browser can still open private, cluster and cloud metadata addresses. Before untrusted clients use the API, add an egress NetworkPolicy that blocks private address ranges.

zh-CN.risk: 只要能用浏览器 API，就可以让服务器去访问内部地址（SSRF）。Browserless 本身可以拦截私有网络，但默认是关闭的。
zh-CN.mitigation: 文件协议、GET 形式的浏览器调用和 CORS 都已关闭。模板没有限制对外连接，浏览器仍然可以访问私有网络、集群内部和云端 metadata 地址。在让不可信的客户端使用 API 之前，请先添加 egress NetworkPolicy，拦截私有地址范围。

zh-TW.risk: 只要能用瀏覽器 API，就可以讓伺服器去連內部網址（SSRF）。Browserless 本身可以擋掉私有網路，但預設是關的。
zh-TW.mitigation: 檔案協定、GET 形式的瀏覽器呼叫和 CORS 都已關閉。範本沒有限制對外連線，瀏覽器仍然可以連到私有網路、叢集內部和雲端 metadata 位址。在讓不受信任的用戶端使用 API 之前，請先加上 egress NetworkPolicy，擋掉私有位址範圍。

risks.risk: Browserless uses an SSPL and commercial dual license. SSPL is not an OSI-approved open source license, and closed-source commercial use is restricted.
risks.mitigation: The template description names the license. Deploying does not give you a license. Check which license applies to you, and ask a lawyer before using it in a commercial product.

zh-CN.risk: Browserless 采用 SSPL 与商业双重许可。SSPL 不是 OSI 认可的开源许可证，闭源的商业用途也受到限制。
zh-CN.mitigation: 模板说明里有写明许可证。部署并不代表你获得了授权。请先确认自己适用哪一种许可证，要用在商业产品时，先咨询法律专业人士。

zh-TW.risk: Browserless 採用 SSPL 與商業雙重授權。SSPL 不是 OSI 認可的開源授權，閉源的商業用途也受到限制。
zh-TW.mitigation: 範本說明裡有寫明授權。部署並不代表你取得了授權。請先確認自己適用哪一種授權，要用在商業產品時，先請教法律專業人士。

risks.risk: One shared token allows powerful automation. It can also show up in client URLs and access logs.
risks.mitigation: The token is generated at deploy time. Send it in the Authorization header where the client supports it. Limit who can read the Kubernetes Secret and the logs. Strip query strings in any external proxy logs. Rotate the token if it leaks.

zh-CN.risk: 共用的 token 可以执行很强的自动化操作，也可能出现在客户端 URL 和访问日志里。
zh-CN.mitigation: token 在部署时自动生成。客户端支持的话，请改用 Authorization 请求头传送。限制谁能读取 Kubernetes 机密和日志。外部代理的日志要去掉查询字符串。token 一旦泄露就要更换。

zh-TW.risk: 共用的 token 可以執行很強的自動化操作，也可能出現在用戶端網址和存取紀錄裡。
zh-TW.mitigation: token 在部署時自動產生。用戶端支援的話，請改用 Authorization 標頭傳送。限制誰能讀取 Kubernetes 機密和紀錄。外部代理伺服器的紀錄要去掉查詢字串。token 一旦外洩就要更換。

scalability.summary: One stateless instance, four concurrent and four queued sessions; active browser sessions cannot migrate.
blockers: Session and CDP/WebSocket connections are process-local; reconnect/retry policy is the caller responsibility.
CPU, memory and shared-memory usage bound browser concurrency.
No HPA is enabled. More replicas need session-aware routing.
Concurrency is set to four sessions. Load-test the node before you raise it.
Readiness removes the endpoint while the queue is full. The 90-second termination window drains short work only.

upgradeNotes: Before each digest update, check the upstream license, browser security fixes, and changes to the start command, paths or UID. Keep the previous digest for rollback.
Drain/reconnect clients before replacing the Pod; running browser sessions and ephemeral downloads are lost.
No persistent browser profiles, cookies, metrics or downloads are retained; export any needed artifacts through the authenticated API before restart.
The only state to back up is the token in browserless-secrets. Back it up with access control. Rotate the token if a browser compromise or a log exposed it.

metadata.name: CLIProxyAPI
metadata.description: Authenticated OpenAI/Gemini-compatible API proxy with private OAuth onboarding and management.

inputs.name: apiKey
inputs.description: Client Bearer API key for /v1 requests. Provider credentials are separate.

inputs.name: managementKey
inputs.description: Management API key; management remains localhost-only and never receives public ingress.

security.summary: CLIProxyAPI runs as a restricted non-root workload. The root filesystem is read-only, there is no service-account token, and extra capabilities are dropped. HTTPS ingress comes only from Traefik. Outbound traffic is not limited.

zh-CN.summary: CLIProxyAPI 以受限的非 root 身份运行。根文件系统只读，没有服务账号 token，多余的权限也都去掉了。HTTPS 流量只从 Traefik 进来。对外连接没有限制。

zh-TW.summary: CLIProxyAPI 以受限的非 root 身分執行。根檔案系統唯讀，沒有服務帳號 token，多餘的權限也都拿掉了。HTTPS 流量只從 Traefik 進來。對外連線沒有限制。

risks.risk: OAuth refresh tokens give access to your upstream provider accounts. The provider's subscription terms may also limit proxying.
risks.mitigation: Use only accounts that you own and are allowed to proxy. The credentials sit on the private PVC, so encrypt any backup of it. Sign in with the native device login through kubectl exec. The callback ports are not exposed.

zh-CN.risk: OAuth refresh token 可以访问你在上游服务商的账号。服务商的订阅条款也可能不允许转接代理。
zh-CN.mitigation: 只使用你自己拥有、并且允许代理的账号。凭证放在私有的 PVC 上，备份时要加密。请通过 kubectl exec 用原生的设备登录来完成授权。回调端口没有对外开放。

zh-TW.risk: OAuth refresh token 可以存取你在上游服務商的帳號。服務商的訂閱條款也可能不允許轉接代理。
zh-TW.mitigation: 只使用你自己擁有、而且允許代理的帳號。憑證放在私有的 PVC 上，備份時要加密。請透過 kubectl exec 用原生的裝置登入來完成授權。回呼連接埠沒有對外開放。

risks.risk: API keys can use up your account quotas. The management interface can read and change sensitive proxy settings.
risks.mitigation: Client keys and management keys are generated separately. The ingress exposes only /v1 and /v1beta. Remote management and the downloadable control panel are turned off. To manage the proxy, run kubectl -n NAMESPACE port-forward deployment/cliproxyapi 8317:8317 --address 127.0.0.1 and do not publish the tunnel.

zh-CN.risk: API 密钥会消耗你账号的额度。管理界面可以读取和修改敏感的代理设置。
zh-CN.mitigation: 客户端密钥和管理密钥是分开生成的。Ingress 只开放 /v1 和 /v1beta。远程管理和可下载的控制面板都已关闭。要管理时，请执行 kubectl -n NAMESPACE port-forward deployment/cliproxyapi 8317:8317 --address 127.0.0.1，并且不要把这个隧道公开出去。

zh-TW.risk: API 金鑰會消耗你帳號的額度。管理介面可以讀取和修改敏感的代理設定。
zh-TW.mitigation: 用戶端金鑰和管理金鑰是分開產生的。Ingress 只開放 /v1 和 /v1beta。遠端管理和可下載的控制面板都已關閉。要管理時，請執行 kubectl -n NAMESPACE port-forward deployment/cliproxyapi 8317:8317 --address 127.0.0.1，而且不要把這個通道公開出去。

scalability.summary: One replica. On a node-local StorageClass, node loss requires manual recovery from off-node backups.
blockers: More replicas would write the same OAuth file store concurrently.
A node-local StorageClass, such as local-path, has no snapshots. Copy the volume off the node for backups

upgradeNotes: The container runs /CLIProxyAPI/CLIProxyAPI --config /runtime/config.yaml --local-model with v8 configuration. No callback ports or management UI are exposed.
Native OAuth credentials persist under /data/auth on the PVC. Stop the pod and back up that PVC and app-secrets encrypted off-node before digest changes. Test a restore before production use.
Before upgrading, check v8 configuration compatibility, provider terms and the stored token format. A rollback can fail after credentials migrate.

An init container regenerates the runtime config from the template settings and generated keys at each pod start. Management config edits are lost when the pod is replaced. Change settings in the template.

Inference fails until you connect a provider. Run native device-code login with an account you own and are permitted to proxy: kubectl -n NAMESPACE exec -it deployment/cliproxyapi -- /CLIProxyAPI/CLIProxyAPI --config /runtime/config.yaml --codex-device-login --no-browser. Callback-based provider logins need a localhost-only tunnel.

metadata.name: Dify
metadata.description: Dify LLM app development platform with PostgreSQL/pgvector, a Dragonfly queue, a code sandbox and S3 object storage. Dify uses a modified Apache license (https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/main/LICENSE): one workspace only without written permission, and keep the frontend logo and copyright. The Dragonfly engine is BUSL-1.1 (https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/LICENSE.md): offering it to third parties as a hosted service or in-memory data store product needs a separate license.

security.summary: The application, Dragonfly, gateway and proxy pods are restricted. The sandbox gets a narrow, justified exception to the baseline policy. The sandbox and the proxy have no sign-in, so NetworkPolicies limit who can call them: the sandbox can reach only the proxy and DNS. Other outbound traffic is not limited. Secrets are generated, ingress uses TLS, and PostgreSQL/pgvector and Dragonfly are run by operators.

zh-CN.summary: 应用、Dragonfly、网关和代理的 Pod 都是受限的。沙箱只拿到一个有理由的小例外，使用基线级别的策略。沙箱和代理没有登录机制，所以用 NetworkPolicy 限制谁能调用它们：沙箱只能访问代理和 DNS。其他对外连接没有限制。机密都是自动生成的，Ingress 使用 TLS，PostgreSQL/pgvector 和 Dragonfly 由 operator 管理。

zh-TW.summary: 應用程式、Dragonfly、閘道和代理的 Pod 都是受限的。沙盒只拿到一個有理由的小例外，使用基準等級的政策。沙盒和代理沒有登入機制，所以用 NetworkPolicy 限制誰能呼叫它們：沙盒只能連到代理和 DNS。其他對外連線沒有限制。機密都是自動產生的，Ingress 使用 TLS，PostgreSQL/pgvector 和 Dragonfly 由 operator 管理。

risks.risk: The Dragonfly engine uses the BUSL-1.1 license, which is source-available. Its Additional Use Grant excludes offering Dragonfly to third parties as a hosted or managed service or as an in-memory data store product.
risks.mitigation: The template description names the license. Use it only within the pinned license grant, or get a separate license. The Apache-2.0 operator does not change the engine's license. The pinned engine version changes to Apache-2.0 on 2030-11-01.

zh-CN.risk: Dragonfly 引擎采用 BUSL-1.1 许可，源码可看但不算开源。它的附加使用授权不允许你把 Dragonfly 作为托管服务或内存数据库产品提供给第三方。
zh-CN.mitigation: 模板说明里有写明许可证。请只在固定版本的授权范围内使用，或另外获得授权。Apache-2.0 的 operator 并不会改变引擎的许可。固定的引擎版本会在 2030-11-01 改为 Apache-2.0。

zh-TW.risk: Dragonfly 引擎採用 BUSL-1.1 授權，原始碼可看但不算開源。它的額外使用授權不允許你把 Dragonfly 當成託管服務或記憶體資料庫產品提供給第三方。
zh-TW.mitigation: 範本說明裡有寫明授權。請只在固定版本的授權範圍內使用，或另外取得授權。Apache-2.0 的 operator 並不會改變引擎的授權。固定的引擎版本會在 2030-11-01 改成 Apache-2.0。

risks.risk: Dragonfly keeps data in memory only, until you turn on snapshots. A restart loses queued or unacknowledged tasks, locks and cache.
risks.mitigation: Turn on Dragonfly backups in Zeabur. DB0 (cache) and DB1 (Celery) stay separate, and cache_mode=false stops the queue from being evicted. Before a restart, stop beat and the producers, and let the workers finish their jobs. After it, check that jobs ran once and only once. Old Valkey AOF, RDB or PVC data is not imported.

zh-CN.risk: Dragonfly 的数据只放在内存里，除非你开启快照。重启后，排队中或还没确认的任务、锁和缓存都会丢失。
zh-CN.mitigation: 请在 Zeabur 开启 Dragonfly 备份。DB0（缓存）和 DB1（Celery）是分开的，cache_mode=false 可以避免队列被清掉。重启前，先停掉 beat 和产生任务的程序，让 worker 把手上的工作做完。重启后，要检查任务有没有漏跑或重跑。旧的 Valkey AOF、RDB 或 PVC 数据不会被导入。

zh-TW.risk: Dragonfly 的資料只放在記憶體裡，除非你開啟快照。重新啟動後，排隊中或還沒確認的任務、鎖和快取都會不見。
zh-TW.mitigation: 請在 Zeabur 開啟 Dragonfly 備份。DB0（快取）和 DB1（Celery）是分開的，cache_mode=false 可以避免佇列被清掉。重新啟動前，先停掉 beat 和產生任務的程式，讓 worker 把手上的工作做完。重啟後，要檢查任務有沒有漏跑或重跑。舊的 Valkey AOF、RDB 或 PVC 資料不會被匯入。

risks.risk: The sandbox container has CAP_CHOWN and CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. Dify's sandbox hands each Python script to its run user and then opens it as root. With DAC_OVERRIDE, root inside the sandbox can read and write files it does not own in the container.
risks.mitigation: Only the sandbox gets these two, next to SYS_CHROOT, SETUID and SETGID. It still drops all other capabilities, allows no privilege escalation, and runs user code as a separate user under the upstream seccomp filter.

zh-CN.risk: 沙箱容器有 CAP_CHOWN 和 CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE 权限。Dify 的沙箱会把每个 Python 脚本交给运行用的用户，再以 root 打开它。有了 DAC_OVERRIDE，沙箱里的 root 就能读写容器内不属于它的文件。
zh-CN.mitigation: 只有沙箱拿到这两个权限，另外还有 SYS_CHROOT、SETUID 和 SETGID。其他权限全部去掉，也不允许提升权限，用户的代码会以另一个用户身份，在上游的 seccomp 过滤下运行。

zh-TW.risk: 沙盒容器有 CAP_CHOWN 和 CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE 權限。Dify 的沙盒會把每個 Python 腳本交給執行用的使用者，再以 root 開啟它。有了 DAC_OVERRIDE，沙盒裡的 root 就能讀寫容器內不屬於它的檔案。
zh-TW.mitigation: 只有沙盒拿到這兩個權限，另外還有 SYS_CHROOT、SETUID 和 SETGID。其他權限全部拿掉，也不允許提升權限，使用者的程式碼會以另一個使用者身分，在上游的 seccomp 過濾下執行。

risks.risk: Dify's trigger and debug Lua scripts access keys that they did not declare in KEYS.
risks.mitigation: Dragonfly runs with allow-undeclared-keys. These scripts run one at a time, so they can lower queue throughput.

zh-CN.risk: Dify 的触发和调试用 Lua 脚本，会访问没有在 KEYS 里声明的 key。
zh-CN.mitigation: Dragonfly 以 allow-undeclared-keys 运行。这些脚本一次只跑一个，可能会让队列的处理速度变慢。

zh-TW.risk: Dify 的觸發和除錯用 Lua 腳本，會存取沒有在 KEYS 裡宣告的 key。
zh-TW.mitigation: Dragonfly 以 allow-undeclared-keys 執行。這些腳本一次只跑一個，可能會讓佇列的處理速度變慢。

risks.risk: Until Dify is set up, the first visitor can create the owner account. The console is also reachable by anyone on the internet.
risks.mitigation: Dify asks for INIT_PASSWORD, generated in dify-secrets/init-password, before it creates the first administrator. A visitor cannot claim the instance without it. Right after the deploy, open /install, enter that password and create the owner. The console is open to anyone who can reach the domain, and Dify has its own sign-in. To limit who can reach it, add an IP limit in the service's network settings.

zh-CN.risk: Dify 在完成初始设置之前，第一个来的访客就能创建所有者账号。任何人从互联网也都能访问控制台。
zh-CN.mitigation: Dify 在创建第一个管理员之前，会要求输入 INIT_PASSWORD，这个密码生成在 dify-secrets/init-password。没有它，访客就抢不走这个实例。部署完成后，请马上打开 /install，输入这个密码并创建所有者。任何能访问该域名的人都能打开控制台，Dify 本身有登录机制。想限制谁能访问，请在服务的网络设置里添加 IP 限制。

zh-TW.risk: Dify 在完成初始設定之前，第一個來的訪客就能建立擁有者帳號。任何人從網際網路也都連得到控制台。
zh-TW.mitigation: Dify 在建立第一個管理員之前，會要求輸入 INIT_PASSWORD，這組密碼產生在 dify-secrets/init-password。沒有它，訪客就搶不走這個實例。部署完成後，請馬上打開 /install，輸入這組密碼並建立擁有者。任何連得到網域的人都能開啟控制台，Dify 本身有登入機制。想限制誰能連進來，請在服務的網路設定裡加上 IP 限制。

risks.risk: The Dify license restricts running more than one workspace and changing the frontend branding.
risks.mitigation: The template description names the license. Use one workspace unless you have written permission from upstream. The frontend images are unmodified, so they keep the branding.

zh-CN.risk: Dify 的许可限制你开多个工作区，也限制修改前端的品牌标识。
zh-CN.mitigation: 模板说明里有写明许可证。除非取得上游的书面许可，否则只使用一个工作区。前端镜像没有被修改，所以品牌标识都保留着。

zh-TW.risk: Dify 的授權限制你開多個工作區，也限制修改前端的品牌標示。
zh-TW.mitigation: 範本說明裡有寫明授權。除非取得上游的書面許可，否則只使用一個工作區。前端映像檔沒有被修改，所以品牌標示都保留著。

risks.risk: The sandbox runs code that other people write, and the SSRF proxy has no sign-in. A pod in the same namespace could call either one.
risks.mitigation: Each has an ingress NetworkPolicy that lets in only the Dify API, worker and beat pods. The sandbox can also reach only the proxy and DNS. These are the only NetworkPolicies in the template. Namespace isolation covers everything else.

zh-CN.risk: 沙箱会运行别人写的代码，SSRF 代理又没有登录机制。同一个命名空间里的任何 Pod 都有可能调用它们。
zh-CN.mitigation: 两者各有一条 ingress NetworkPolicy，只放行 Dify 的 API、worker 和 beat Pod 进来。沙箱也只能访问代理和 DNS。模板里只有这几条 NetworkPolicy，其余的部分靠命名空间隔离。

zh-TW.risk: 沙盒會執行別人寫的程式，SSRF 代理又沒有登入機制。同一個命名空間裡的任何 Pod 都有可能呼叫它們。
zh-TW.mitigation: 兩者各有一條 ingress NetworkPolicy，只放行 Dify 的 API、worker 和 beat Pod 進來。沙盒也只能連到代理和 DNS。範本裡只有這幾條 NetworkPolicy，其餘的部分靠命名空間隔離。

risks.risk: The code runner needs root to set up a chroot and to switch to a unique identity for each run.
risks.mitigation: This is the only exception to the baseline policy. It gets minimal capabilities, RuntimeDefault, and the upstream inner seccomp filter. It also has a generated API key, a pod with no database credentials, egress to the proxy only, and bounded resources.

zh-CN.risk: 代码运行器需要 root，才能建立 chroot，并在每次运行时切换成独立的身份。
zh-CN.mitigation: 这是基线策略唯一的例外。它只拿到最少的权限，使用 RuntimeDefault 和上游内层的 seccomp 过滤。API 密钥是自动生成的，Pod 里没有数据库凭证，对外只能访问代理，资源也有上限。

zh-TW.risk: 程式執行器需要 root，才能建立 chroot，並在每次執行時切換成獨立的身分。
zh-TW.mitigation: 這是基準政策唯一的例外。它只拿到最少的權限，使用 RuntimeDefault 和上游內層的 seccomp 過濾。API 金鑰是自動產生的，Pod 裡沒有資料庫憑證，對外只能連到代理，資源也有上限。

risks.risk: Plugins are third-party code that you trust. They can use the model integrations you have configured.
risks.mitigation: Keep FORCE_VERIFYING_SIGNATURE set to true. The remote debugging and remote install listener are turned off. Let only trusted administrators install plugins. All plugins share one trust boundary, and the plugin pod has a restricted identity.

zh-CN.risk: 插件是你要信任的第三方代码，可以使用你配置好的模型集成。
zh-CN.mitigation: 请让 FORCE_VERIFYING_SIGNATURE 保持 true。远程调试和远程安装的监听都已关闭。只让可信的管理员安装插件。所有插件共用同一个信任范围，插件 Pod 的身份也受到限制。

zh-TW.risk: 外掛是你要信任的第三方程式，可以使用你設定好的模型整合。
zh-TW.mitigation: 請讓 FORCE_VERIFYING_SIGNATURE 維持 true。遠端除錯和遠端安裝的監聽都已關閉。只讓信任的管理員安裝外掛。所有外掛共用同一個信任範圍，外掛 Pod 的身分也受到限制。

risks.risk: The PostgreSQL manager (CloudNativePG instance manager) needs limited permissions on the Kubernetes API.
risks.mitigation: Use the catalog operator and its limited service account.

zh-CN.risk: PostgreSQL 的管理程序（CloudNativePG instance manager）需要 Kubernetes API 的部分权限。
zh-CN.mitigation: 请使用目录里的 operator 和它权限受限的服务账号。

zh-TW.risk: PostgreSQL 的管理程式（CloudNativePG instance manager）需要 Kubernetes API 的部分權限。
zh-TW.mitigation: 請使用目錄裡的 operator 和它權限受限的服務帳號。

scalability.summary: One instance per trusted owner; do not horizontally scale this deployment.
blockers: One API migrator, one beat scheduler, single Dragonfly instance, plugin state on one RWO volume, and one supported licensed workspace.
External S3 object storage must exist. A node-local StorageClass has no HA or snapshots.

upgradeNotes: The dify-api pod has INIT_PASSWORD from dify-secrets/init-password. The /install page asks for it before it creates the owner.
Database backups are off when the template is installed. To turn them on, open the database in Zeabur and use the Backups tab.

The console is open on the domain; add an IP limit in the service's network settings if you need one. The Dify license still limits you to one workspace unless separately authorized; keep frontend logos and copyright unchanged.

From Dify 1.13: back up the database first, because migration 5578e028b2f2 (1.17.1) cannot be reversed. Scale dify-worker and dify-beat to 0 before the upgrade, so that old workers do not take new queue entries; the API migrates the database at start. Then run `flask backfill-plugin-auto-upgrade` once in dify-api (1.15), or plugin auto-upgrade settings stop working. Keep PASSWORD_PEPPER unset: setting it makes every existing password fail. The plugin daemon now migrates its own database at start.
Sandbox 0.2.15 runs each Python and JavaScript execution under its own UID. Check code-runner protocol and syscall changes during upgrades.

Preserve CNPG application credentials, generated encryption/queue/sandbox Secrets, PostgreSQL backups, external S3 documents/keys, and plugin storage PVC before updates. The Dify app key and the S3 key objects are needed to decrypt model provider configuration. Stop writers before filesystem exports.

PostgreSQL uses the CNPG standard image with pgvector as the vector store. To migrate an existing instance that uses Weaviate, reindex its data into pgvector. Do not change the PostgreSQL major version with an image-only rollout; migrate logically or use a CNPG major upgrade.
Application object storage is an existing S3-compatible bucket with your credentials. To migrate an existing instance, copy its objects into the bucket.

Only API runs migrations; beat remains a single scheduler; plugin storage remains a single-node PVC. Preserve queue credentials and DB0/DB1 separation; stop beat/producers, drain workers and checkpoint before cutover. Reconcile lost/replayed tasks and expired locks after recovery. Old Valkey AOF, RDB or PVC data is not imported. Dragonfly does not provide Redis Stack modules; data that depends on them needs a separate migration.
Dragonfly is BUSL-1.1. Offering third parties a hosted/managed Dragonfly or an in-memory data store product needs a separate license.
